info.name: GeoMineX API — v1
info.description:
Every implemented `/api/v1` route, Phase 1 and Phase 2 — PRD §13. Twelve folders in the order a first run should follow: Infrastructure, Auth, Users, Subsidiaries, Documents, Reports, Dashboard, Queries, Topics, Analytics, Audit, Failure scenarios.

`PATCH /extracted-fields/:id` lives in the **Documents** folder rather than one of its own: it is mounted at its own path (§10.2) but it is an operation on a document that has already been processed, and separating it hides the upload → process → review → override sequence the folder exists to show.

## What each folder contains

The happy path for every route, followed by the §9.9 failure modes that actually apply to it, each as its own request:

- `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — a SHAPE failure, caught by Zod before any service runs. Carries `error.fields`.
- `400 INVALID_REQUEST` — schema-valid but logically invalid (a range ending before it starts, a retry on a document that did not fail, a review of an answer that does not exist yet). No `fields` map, because nothing is wrong with the shape.
- `400 CONFIRM_TEXT_MISMATCH` / `409 CONFLICT` — where a typed confirmation or a uniqueness constraint exists.
- `401` missing token, and `401` expired or revoked token as a separate request, because `UNAUTHORIZED` and `TOKEN_EXPIRED` mean different things to a frontend.
- `403` where a role gate exists.
- `404 unknown id` **and** `404 out-of-scope id`, always as **two** requests. Their responses are identical on purpose: PRD §9.1 forbids telling a caller that a resource exists in a subsidiary they cannot reach, so the collection has to show the pair to make that convention visible.
- `429` where a stricter limiter applies (`aiLimiter` on asks and retries, `analyticsLimiter` shared by Topics and Analytics).

Where a mode is absent, the folder description says why — no role gate on Dashboard/Topics/Analytics, no path parameter to be unknown, no uniqueness constraint — rather than leaving a silent gap. Test scripts assert the envelope shape and, on failures, `error.code`.

## First run

1. `npm run seed`, then start the dev server. Select the **GeoMineX — Local** environment: the request chain writes to environment scope, which outranks collection scope.
2. **Auth** → `Request sign-in code`, copy the code from the server log into `otpCode`, then `Verify code`. That captures `accessToken` and `userId`.
3. **Subsidiaries** → `List subsidiaries` captures `subsidiaryId`. Run `Create subsidiary` and paste the new id into `otherSubsidiaryId` by hand — the out-of-scope requests need a second one.
4. **Documents** → upload a file, then re-send `GET /documents/:id` until `status` is `validated`. Chunks, extracted fields, report drafting and query answers all depend on reaching that state.
5. Everything else runs in folder order.

## Two asynchronous contracts

Neither endpoint returns its result in the response that creates the work:

- `POST /documents` returns **201 `queued`**. OCR and extraction run in a worker; poll `GET /documents/:id`.
- `POST /queries` returns **201 `queued` with `responseText: null` and `citations: []`**. The answer is produced by a worker and collected by polling `GET /queries/:id`. Running the Queries folder top to bottom and stopping at the 201 does not mean the answer is missing — it has not been generated yet. The Queries folder description explains why the endpoint is built this way.

## Identities the failure requests need

Four environment variables are access tokens for people other than the admin. Sign in as each and paste their `accessToken`:

- `cilAccessToken` — a `cil_user` granted `{{subsidiaryId}}`. Shows `403` on the admin-only actions (publish a report, approve a query answer) while the resource itself is fully visible to them — which is exactly why those are 403 and not 404.
- `mocAccessToken` — a `moc_official`. Read-only across subsidiaries (§2), so it shows `403` on every write gate.
- `outOfScopeAccessToken` — a non-admin granted only `{{otherSubsidiaryId}}`. Shows the 404-not-403 convention against real, existing ids.
- `expiredAccessToken` — any token past its lifetime, or one whose session was revoked via `DELETE /auth/sessions/:id`.

`unknownId` is a fixed, well-formed ObjectId (`000000000000000000000000`) that exists in no collection — the other half of each 404 pair.

The refresh credential is an HttpOnly cookie: Postman stores and replays it automatically, and it is never exposed to a script.

variable.description: A well-formed ObjectId that exists in no collection. Used by every "404 — unknown id" request, whose response must be indistinguishable from the matching "404 — out-of-scope id" request (PRD §9.1).
Set by POST /reports — the archive confirmation must equal it exactly (§8.3).
A second subsidiary, held only by outOfScopeAccessToken's user.
cil_user granted {{subsidiaryId}} — shows 403 on admin-only actions against a visible resource.
moc_official — read-only across subsidiaries (§2); shows 403 on write gates.
Non-admin granted ONLY {{otherSubsidiaryId}} — shows 404-not-403 on real ids.
A token past its lifetime or whose session was revoked — shows 401 TOKEN_EXPIRED / TOKEN_INVALID.

item.name: 4. Documents
item.description:
Ingestion and traceability — PRD §4.1, §4.5, §5.8, §9.4, §10.2.

Upload is the only multipart route (field name `file`); everything else is JSON. Listing is CURSOR-paginated (§9.8) because the collection takes continuous inserts while a reviewer pages through it — offset paging would silently skip and duplicate rows.

Processing is ASYNCHRONOUS: the upload returns 201 with `status: "queued"`. Poll `GET /documents/:id` until `status` becomes `validated` or `failed`; chunks and extracted fields do not exist until then.

Out-of-scope reads return 404, never 403 (§9.1) — the last two requests in this folder are deliberately kept separate so that convention is visible.

formdata.description: Pick a local PDF / scan / spreadsheet / image. The field name must be exactly `file`; anything else is a 400 VALIDATION_ERROR raised by the controller, not by multer.
Required. Checked against the caller's grants before it reaches a query (§8.3); a subsidiary you do not hold is 404.
Optional operator tags on top of the automatic ones (§4.1). Multipart sends strings, so a comma-separated list and a repeated field are both accepted. Max 10 tags, 40 chars each.

request.description:
PRD §4.1, §9.4. Role gate is `admin` + `cil_user`: MoC officials are read-only across subsidiaries (§2).

The body limit here is `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` enforced by multer, NOT the global 10kb JSON limit — raising the global limit to fit a scanned PDF would remove body-size protection from every JSON endpoint in the system. An oversized file returns 413 `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`.

Returns 201 with the row still `queued`; the OCR/extraction worker fills it in afterwards.

query.description: 1..100, default 25.
The `pagination.nextCursor` from the previous page. Disabled on the first call.
queued | processing | validated | failed
pdf | scan | spreadsheet | image
A string enum 'true'/'false', not a coerced boolean: z.coerce.boolean() treats the literal string 'false' as true, so the parameter would do the opposite of what it says.
Optional narrowing. Always intersected with the caller's grants.
Text search over FILENAME AND TAGS ONLY — never over extracted values (§8.2).

PRD §4.1, §9.4, §9.5. The polling endpoint while the worker runs.

`injectionSuspected` travels to the client so a reviewer knows why a document is in the queue, but `injectionRuleIds` does not — publishing which patterns fired tells an author exactly which ones to avoid. `storageKey` is never serialized either: a client must not be able to construct or guess a storage path.

request.description:
PRD §5.8, §9.4 — the most security-sensitive route in the system. Scope is re-checked on every download and the fetch is audited.

Always sent as an ATTACHMENT with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so an uploaded file can never be rendered inline in the API's own origin. The filename is RFC 5987 encoded, so a crafted filename cannot inject extra header directives.

PRD §5.8, §8.1 — the passage-level half of traceability. Each chunk carries `chunkIndex`, `pageNumber` and `section`, which is exactly the tuple a query citation points at, so the client resolves a citation to its source text without ever parsing prose. Empty until the document reaches `validated`.

PRD §4.1, §4.5. `requiresReview` is derived per field from `OCR_REVIEW_THRESHOLD`: at or below the threshold a figure must not be treated as verified. Captures `extractedFieldId` for the override request below.

PRD §4.5, §9.6, §10.2. Mounted as its own `/extracted-fields/:id` family, not nested under the document, matching the endpoint family the PRD specifies.

`reason` is REQUIRED (3..500 chars): an override is only auditable if the *why* is recorded alongside the who, when and what. The pre-override figure is preserved as `originalValue`, so a correction never destroys the machine reading. Role gate is `admin` + `cil_user` — a read-only MoC official cannot restate a figure.

exec: pm.test('Machine reading is preserved, not destroyed', () => pm.expect(f).to.have.property('originalValue'));

request.description:
PRD §9.7 — retry is an EXPLICIT, authorized, rate-limitable endpoint rather than a hidden internal loop, so a stuck job stays observable.

Only a document whose `status` is `failed` can be retried, and only while attempts remain below the dead-letter ceiling. Point `documentId` at a failed document before running this; against any other status it returns 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` — that case has its own request below. Role gate is `admin` + `cil_user`.

item.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR — limit above the cap, unknown status

query.description: The cap is 100.
Not a document status — that enum belongs to reports.

request.description: PRD §9.2, §9.8. Zod rejects the request before any service sees it, and `error.fields` names each offending path so the client can mark the right input. These query bounds are COST bounds as well as correctness bounds.

item.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR — override with no usable reason

request.description: PRD §4.5. `reason` has a 3-character floor precisely so that "ok" cannot stand in for an audit justification.

item.name: 400 INVALID_REQUEST — retry a document that did not fail

request.description: PRD §9.8. Schema-VALID (a well-formed id) but logically invalid (the document is not in `failed`), which is exactly the split `INVALID_REQUEST` exists for, as distinct from `VALIDATION_ERROR` which is a SHAPE failure. Run this while `documentId` points at a queued or validated document.
PRD §9.1. `documentRouter.use(requireAuth)` sits above every route in the family, so there is no unauthenticated document surface at all.

PRD §9.3, §9.8. Set `expiredAccessToken` to a token past its lifetime, or reuse an access token after revoking its session with `DELETE /auth/sessions/:id`.

An expired signature gives `TOKEN_EXPIRED`; a deactivated user or a revoked session gives `TOKEN_INVALID` with a deliberately generic message, because the response must not reveal WHICH check failed. `TOKEN_EXPIRED` is what lets the frontend tell "refresh normally" apart from "re-authenticate".

formdata.description: Any local file; the role gate refuses before the bytes are read.

request.description:
PRD §2, §9.1. MoC officials are read-only across subsidiaries.

403, NOT 404: reaching a role-gated endpoint means the caller may legitimately know the route exists — only the ACTION is denied. The 404 convention applies to cross-subsidiary RESOURCE access, demonstrated separately below.

item.name: 403 — MoC official cannot override a figure

request.description: PRD §2, §4.5. The role gate runs ahead of the service, so the override is refused without the field ever being loaded.

PRD §9.1. `unknownId` is a well-formed ObjectId that exists nowhere, so it passes schema validation and then misses on the scoped read. Compare the response with the next request — the two are deliberately indistinguishable.

PRD §9.1 — THE CONVENTION THIS PAIR OF REQUESTS EXISTS TO MAKE VISIBLE.

`documentId` is a REAL document living in `{{subsidiaryId}}`. `outOfScopeAccessToken` belongs to a non-admin granted only `{{otherSubsidiaryId}}`. The answer is 404 `NOT_FOUND` — indistinguishable from the previous request's response — and NOT 403, because a 403 here would confirm that a document with this id exists in another subsidiary. The scope clause is folded into the query itself, so the row is never loaded into memory.

Setup: create a second subsidiary and store its id in `otherSubsidiaryId`, invite a `cil_user` with `subsidiaryAccess: ["{{otherSubsidiaryId}}"]`, sign in as them, and store their access token in `outOfScopeAccessToken`.

exec: pm.test('Not 403 — a 403 here would confirm the row exists', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.not.eql(403));

item.name: 5. Reports
item.description:
Report templates and the draft → publish → archive lifecycle — PRD §4.2, §8.1, §8.3, §9.6, §10.2.

Two mount points: `/report-templates` (the shape a report is drafted into) and `/reports` (the drafts themselves).

Unlike documents and the query log, report lists are OFFSET-paginated (`total`, `page`, `limit`, `totalPages`) — §9.8 reserves cursor pagination for append-heavy lists; a filtered report list is stable enough for offsets.

Two separations of duty are visible here: drafting excludes read-only MoC officials (§2), and PUBLISHING is admin-only even though CIL users may draft (§11.5) — the person putting a figure on record is not the person who wrote it.

RUN ORDER NOTE: the archive happy path is the LAST request in this folder, after the `CONFIRM_TEXT_MISMATCH` request. Archiving is terminal, and `archiveReport` rejects an already-archived report with `INVALID_REQUEST` *before* it ever compares the confirmation text — so the mismatch case is only observable while the report is still live.

request.description: PRD §4.2. A template with an empty `subsidiaryScope` is offered to everyone; a scoped template is offered only to users holding one of its subsidiaries. Admins see all. Captures `templateId` for the create-report request.

PRD §4.2. Admin only — a template defines the shape every subsidiary's return is filed in, so it is not a per-subsidiary edit.

`subsidiaryScope: []` means "available to everyone". Names are unique among non-deleted templates; a repeat is 409 `CONFLICT` (its own request below).

query.description: 1-based, default 1.
1..100, default 20.
draft | published | archived
Optional narrowing; always intersected with the caller's grants.
Optional narrowing by template.

request.description: PRD §9.8 — OFFSET pagination here, deliberately unlike documents/queries/audit logs. A filtered report list is a stable set, so `total`, `page`, `limit` and `totalPages` are meaningful and worth having.

PRD §4.2, §8.1. Role gate is `admin` + `cil_user`; drafting is a write, so read-only MoC officials are excluded (§2).

Only `validated` documents may be cited — a report must never cite a file whose processing failed. A source document that is out of scope or unknown is 404 (its own request below); one that is in scope but not validated is 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`.

Citations come back as STRUCTURED METADATA (`documentId`, `chunkIndex`, `pageNumber`, `section`, `confidenceScore`), separate from the prose (§8.1) — the client never parses a section body to find a source. `hasUnreviewedFigures` flags a draft that leans on a low-confidence extraction.
PRD §4.2, §5.8. `sourceDocumentLinks` and `citations` are the traceability path back to `GET /documents/:id/chunks`.

PRD §4.2, §9.6. Every edit snapshots the previous section text with its `changeSummary`, so a published figure can be traced back to the wording it replaced. Read-only for every role that can see the report.

PRD §4.2, §9.6. Role gate is `admin` + `cil_user`.

Only DRAFTS can be edited: once published, a report is on record and editing it returns 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` (its own request below). Each accepted edit bumps `currentVersion` and appends to the version history.

PRD §4.2, §11.5 — SEPARATION OF DUTIES. Admin only, deliberately not open to the CIL users who draft: in a system whose output feeds parliamentary answers, the person writing a figure is not the person putting it on record.

200, not 201: an action-style POST that creates no new resource (§10.3). `publishedBy` and `publishedAt` are recorded and the transition is audited.

item.name: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR — draft with no source documents

request.description: PRD §4.2, §9.2. An empty title and an empty source list are both SHAPE failures. `sourceDocumentIds` has a floor of 1 by design: a report with no cited source has nothing to trace back to (§5.8).

PRD §4.2, §9.8. Run this AFTER the publish request above. The body is perfectly well-formed — the request is refused because of the report's STATE, which is what `INVALID_REQUEST` means as opposed to `VALIDATION_ERROR`.

This is the rule that keeps a published figure from being restated in place with no version trail.

item.name: 400 CONFIRM_TEXT_MISMATCH — archive without typing the title

request.description:
PRD §8.3, §9.8. Archiving is irreversible in effect, so it takes TYPED confirmation: `confirm` must equal the report's exact title, not a generic "yes". A dedicated `CONFIRM_TEXT_MISMATCH` code (not a plain validation error) lets the frontend tell the user precisely what to retype.

Must run BEFORE the archive happy path below: once archived, the already-archived check fires first and returns `INVALID_REQUEST` instead.
PRD §9.1. Both routers mount `requireAuth` before any route, so neither reports nor templates have an unauthenticated surface.
PRD §9.3. See the Documents folder for how to populate `expiredAccessToken`.

item.name: 403 — MoC official cannot draft a report

request.description: PRD §2, §9.1. Drafting is a write; MoC officials are read-only across subsidiaries. 403 because the route is legitimately visible to them — only the action is denied.

item.name: 403 — CIL user may draft but may not publish

request.description:
PRD §11.5 — the separation of duties, seen from the other side. `cilAccessToken` belongs to a `cil_user` who HOLDS `{{subsidiaryId}}`, so the report is fully visible to them and they may edit it; publishing is still refused.

That is exactly why this is 403 and not 404: the resource is legitimately theirs to see, and only the ACTION is out of reach.

exec: pm.test('FORBIDDEN — the row is visible, the action is not', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.code).to.eql('FORBIDDEN'));

request.description: PRD §9.1. A well-formed ObjectId that exists nowhere. Compare with the next request.

PRD §9.1. A REAL report in `{{subsidiaryId}}`, read by a non-admin granted only `{{otherSubsidiaryId}}`. Same 404 as the unknown-id request above — the caller is never told the report exists somewhere else.

Contrast this with the CIL-user publish request higher up: same 4xx family, opposite code, because there the resource was in scope and only the action was denied.

item.name: 404 — source document unknown or out of scope

request.description: PRD §9.1, §8.3. Client-supplied document ids are resolved through a SCOPED query, so an unchecked id never reaches a Mongo filter. A source document that does not exist and one that lives in another subsidiary produce the same 404 — the response cannot be used to probe for documents outside the caller's grants.
PRD §9.8. Re-sends the exact name created earlier in this folder. Template names are unique among non-deleted templates, so two returns can never be filed under indistinguishable shapes.

PRD §8.3, §9.6. Admin only, and `confirm` must equal the report's exact title — captured as `reportTitle` by the create request above.

Deliberately the last request in this folder: archiving is terminal, and once it succeeds the `CONFIRM_TEXT_MISMATCH` case above becomes unobservable (the already-archived check returns `INVALID_REQUEST` first). Re-running this request against the same report returns 400 `INVALID_REQUEST` for that reason.

item.name: 6. Dashboard
item.description:
The §5.3 leadership snapshot — PRD §4.6, §5.3, §10.2.

Two GETs, no parameters, no role gate: every role may see a dashboard, and what differs is WHAT IS IN IT. Scoping is implicit and total — the cache key is derived from the caller's GRANT LIST (never from their user id), so a user can never read an aggregate computed over subsidiaries they cannot access, and a user whose grants change gets a different key rather than a stale over-broad answer.

Because there is no path parameter and no role gate, the §9.9 modes that apply here are 401 only: there is no id to be unknown or out of scope, and no action to be forbidden. The third request below shows the scoping that stands in for a 404.

Every figure travels with `computedAt` and `cached` (§4.6): a stale number presented as live is a traceability defect, so freshness is part of the payload rather than something the client has to guess.

request.description:
PRD §5.3. Four blocks in one round trip: `quickStats` (the three §1.5 headline percentages plus `computedAt`/`cached`), `documents` counts, `recentReports`, and `pendingWork`.

`pendingWork` unions two halves authorized by DIFFERENT rules and that is deliberate: documents are filtered by the caller's grants on a top-level `subsidiaryId`, while queries use the containment clause imported from the queries module — a query answered over {A, B} is hidden from a user who holds only A, because its prose may carry B's figures.

exec: pm.test('Headline percentages are numbers, never nulls here', () => {

request.description:
PRD §4.6, §5.3. The quick-stat numbers on their own, for polling a card without refetching recent reports and the pending-work queue.

Run it twice: the first call recomputes and returns `cached: false`, the second is served from `MetricsCache` within `METRICS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS` and returns `cached: true` with the SAME `computedAt`. The cache key folds in the payload version and the assumption fingerprint, so retuning a metric constant can never serve figures computed under the old assumptions for a full TTL.

item.name: GET /dashboard as a scoped user (implicit isolation)

request.description:
PRD §9.1, §4.6 — what stands in for a 404 on a route with no id.

The same URL, a different caller. `outOfScopeAccessToken` holds only `{{otherSubsidiaryId}}`, so this 200 covers a strictly smaller corpus than the admin's. Compare `documents.total` with the first request's: the difference IS the isolation. Nothing in the response names a subsidiary the caller cannot access, and the cached row backing it was keyed on this caller's grants, so it can never be the admin's aggregate served back.

exec: pm.test('Status 200 — every role gets a dashboard', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('Scoped totals, not the global ones', () => pm.expect(d.documents.total).to.be.a('number'));
pm.test('Recent reports stay inside the caller grants', () => pm.expect(d.recentReports).to.be.an('array'));

request.description: PRD §9.1. `dashboardRouter.use(requireAuth)` covers both routes. There is no anonymous view of the leadership figures.

PRD §9.3. `requireAuth` re-checks live state the token cannot know about — whether the user is still active and whether the session behind the token was revoked — so a force-logout takes effect immediately rather than at token expiry.

item.name: 7. Queries
item.description:
The parliamentary query log — PRD §4.4, §5.7, §8.1, §9.5, §9.6, §10.2, §10.3.

### READ THIS BEFORE RUNNING THE FOLDER TOP TO BOTTOM

`POST /queries` is **asynchronous**. It returns **201 with `status: "queued"` and `responseText: null`** — no answer is produced inside the request. The answer arrives later, from the worker, and you collect it by **polling `GET /queries/:id`** until `status` reaches a terminal value (`answered`, `unsupported`, `failed` or `dead_lettered`).

If you run this folder in one pass and stop at the 201, **the answer is not missing — it has not been generated yet.** Re-send `GET /queries/:id` a few times.

### Why it is built this way

Retrieval plus generation is unbounded work; doing it in the request would hold an HTTP connection open for as long as the model takes and make the endpoint a denial-of-service lever with a valid token. The queued row is also what makes the pipeline observable: `status`, `attempts` and `failureReason` are all readable while it runs, and `GET /analytics` reports `queriesQueued` / `queriesInFlight` / `queriesDeadLettered`.

### Two rules worth watching

- **Containment, not intersection (§9.1).** A query answered over {A, B} may carry B's figures in its prose, so a user granted only A must not read it — even though the query "touches" a subsidiary they hold. That is why the happy path below pins `subsidiaryId` explicitly.
- **Citations are never client-authored (§9.5).** The review schema has no `citations` field at all; a citation can only ever be derived from the chunks actually retrieved. The "citations in the body are ignored" request proves it.

`POST /queries` and `POST /queries/:id/retry` sit behind `aiLimiter` (12/min, keyed on the USER), stricter than the global limit as §9.2 requires.

item.name: POST /queries (201 QUEUED — the answer comes later)

request.description:
PRD §4.4, §5.7, §9.2, §10.3. All three roles may ask — §2 gives the MoC Official the query interface explicitly, and asking writes only the caller's own question, never subsidiary data.

**201 with the row still `queued`. `responseText` is `null` and `citations` is `[]` at this point — that is correct, not a bug.** Poll `GET /queries/:id` (next request) for the answer.

Fields:
- `questionText` — 10..2000 chars, sized so a maximal body stays well inside the global 10kb JSON limit, which the body parser enforces BEFORE validation runs.
- `isParliamentary` — the answer STYLE is derived from this flag in the worker, so there is no separate `style` field the two could disagree about.
- `subsidiaryId` — optional; omitted means every subsidiary the caller holds (all of them, for an admin). **Pinned here deliberately**: it makes `contextScope.subsidiaryIds` a single id, which is what lets the 403 and 404 requests further down demonstrate containment cleanly.
- `documentIds` — optional, max 25. Narrows retrieval to named, in-scope, VALIDATED documents. Out of scope is 404; in scope but unvalidated is 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`.

exec: pm.test('Queued, not answered — the worker has not run yet', () => {
pm.test('Context scope is resolved at ask time (§9.1)', () => {
console.log('Queued query ' + q.id + ' — now poll GET /queries/:id until status is answered/unsupported/failed.');

item.name: GET /queries/:id (POLL THIS until status is terminal)

request.description:
PRD §4.4, §8.1, §9.5 — **this is where the answer appears.** Send it repeatedly; `status` walks `queued` → `retrieving` → `answering` → `answered` | `unsupported` | `failed` (→ `dead_lettered` once retries are exhausted).

What comes back once it is terminal:
- `responseText` — the generated prose.
- `citations` — STRUCTURED metadata (`documentId`, `pageNumber`, `chunkIndex`, `section`, `quote`, `relevance`). The client links these into the §5.8 traceability routes and NEVER parses `responseText` to find a source (§8.1).
- `retrieval` — `candidatesConsidered`, `passagesUsed`, `passagesWithheld`, `discardedCitations`. The counts make the answer auditable.
- `warnings` — human-readable LOSS. A passage withheld because it contained suspected embedded instructions is visible loss, never silent loss (§9.5); so is a proposed citation discarded for not matching the sources actually retrieved.
- `answerStatus: "unsupported"` — an honest "no authorised source in scope supports an answer", which is a correct outcome rather than a failure.

`retrievedChunkIds` and `injectionFlags` are internal and surface only as COUNTS: publishing which rules fired tells an attacker which patterns to avoid.

exec: pm.test('Status is a known pipeline state', () => pm.expect(['queued', 'retrieving', 'answering', 'answered', 'unsupported', 'failed', 'dead_lettered']).to.include(q.status));
pm.test('Citations are structured metadata, not prose (§8.1)', () => pm.expect(q.citations).to.be.an('array'));

item.description:
Word cloud, clustering and term trend — PRD §4.3, §5.6, §9.2, §10.2.

ONE route: `GET /api/v1/topics`. All three roles may read it (§2 gives MoC officials analytics), so there is no `roleGuard` — a guard listing every role is a guard that only ever goes stale. That means **403 is not an applicable failure mode here**; the isolation is enforced instead by folding the caller's grants into every pipeline AND into the cache key.

Dates are IST **CALENDAR** dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never instants. The client never sends a timestamp, so the client can never disagree with the server about where an Indian fiscal quarter begins; the service converts each date into the half-open UTC window the pipelines actually match on and returns BOTH forms (`from`/`to` and `fromUtc`/`toUtc`) so a figure is reproducible.

The two 400s are different animals and both are represented below: a malformed date is a SHAPE failure (`VALIDATION_ERROR`), while a range that ends before it starts is schema-valid and logically invalid (`INVALID_REQUEST`) — §9.8's own worked example.

Every bound (`limit`, `minSources`, the range ceiling) is a COST bound as well as a correctness one: a cold-cache request here is the heaviest read in the system, which is why the route sits behind `analyticsLimiter` rather than the global limit.

item.name: 9. Analytics
item.description:
The series and breakdown behind the §5.3 dashboard — PRD §4.6, §7.7, §9.2, §9.8, §10.2.

ONE route: `GET /api/v1/analytics`. Where `GET /dashboard` gives one snapshot, this gives the same figures BUCKETED over time, broken down by subsidiary, with the queue health and the assumptions used to compute them.

All three roles, so no `roleGuard` and **no applicable 403** — §2 grants MoC officials analytics explicitly, and a CIL user sees only their own subsidiaries because the scope clause sits inside every pipeline AND inside the cache key. - `null` is used honestly. A `null` block means the caller did not ASK for it via `include`; a `null` percentage means there was no evidence either way. Neither is the same as zero. (The dashboard snapshot deliberately differs: it reports 0 rather than null, because a card cannot render an absence.)

Dates are IST calendar dates, exactly as in Topics; `fromUtc`/`toUtc` come back alongside so every figure is reproducible.

item.description: Cursor-paginated: offset paging would skip rows as new ones arrive.

item.name: 11. Failure scenarios
item.description:
Cross-cutting failures that belong to no single resource — the shared middleware layer: authentication, the global validator, the NoSQL-operator guard, the catch-all 404, and the auth rate limiter.

The PER-ENDPOINT §9.9 coverage is NOT here. Each resource folder carries its own failure requests (400 VALIDATION_ERROR, 400 INVALID_REQUEST, 401 missing, 401 expired, 403 wrong role, 404 unknown id, 404 out-of-scope id, 409, 429) immediately after its happy paths, because a mode only means something against the endpoint that can fail in it.

request.description: A subsidiary you do not hold returns 404, never 403 — 403 would confirm it exists.

item.name: 429 — auth rate limit (send 11x in a minute)
